paper_summary: Japanese-language short paper (J. Marine Acoust. Soc. Jpn.) measuring the temperature dependence of longitudinal sound velocity of three commercial Trelleborg Applied Technologies syntactic foams (TG-26/3000, TG-28/4000, TG-39/11500, depth ratings 3000/4000/11500 m) and of Fluorinert FC-72, for use as the solid lens and inner liquid of a convex acoustic lens mounted on an AUV bow. Sound velocity was measured with the sing-around method at 500 kHz and 1 MHz between 10 and 30 C; velocity decreases linearly with temperature for every material and increases with foam density (2475-2805 m/s at 500 kHz). From the fitted acoustic impedances the best sea-water / solid-lens / FC-72 combination was TG-28/4000 (total transmittance 0.965 at both frequencies). No mechanical properties (modulus, strength) are reported.

extraction_notes: Paper is in Japanese (English abstract, tables and figure captions). It is on-topic (three commercial syntactic foams) but it is an acoustics study: the only measured quantities are longitudinal sound velocity, its temperature coefficient, acoustic impedance, refractive index relative to sea water and transmittance - none of which exist in the schema. Consequently every record carries only measured_density_g_cc (converted from kg/m3: 416 -> 0.416, 448 -> 0.448, 639 -> 0.639) and all acoustic numbers are preserved verbatim in microstructure_notes. The densities are the manufacturer nominal values (公称値, Table 1), not measured by the authors; sound velocities are the authors' own measurements, so records are marked primary. One record per material per test frequency (500 kHz, 1 MHz) as required by the one-record-per-test-condition rule; the schema fields are therefore identical within each material pair and differ only in the noted acoustic values. Matrix class, particle type and process route are not stated anywhere in the paper for these proprietary Trelleborg TG-series foams, so all three enums are set to 'other' rather than assuming an epoxy/glass-microballoon system. Test temperature is left null because each row is an average/fit over the 10-30 C sweep (Table 3 values are model estimates at the 18.93 C Suruga Bay annual mean, noted in microstructure_notes). Fluorinert FC-72 (density 1680 kg/m3, velocity ~528 m/s) and sea water are not hollow-particle composites and get no records. No modulus, strength, strain, or thermal property is reported anywhere in the paper.
